items.stem: State any three stages of the entrepreneurial journey.
items.answer: Self-discovery; Identifying opportunities; Generating and selecting ideas; Preparing a business plan; Mobilising resources; Launching the enterprise; Growth and scaling up
items.markingKey: Any three of: Self-discovery; Identifying opportunities; Generating and selecting ideas; Preparing a business plan; Mobilising resources; Launching the enterprise; Growth and scaling up (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain "Finding customers" with reference to the challenges faced in the entrepreneurial journey.
items.answer: Finding customers: Convincing people to try a new product.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Convincing people to try a new product.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Scaling up is a stage of the entrepreneurial journey.
Reason (R): A successful venture expands its operations and markets.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Pooja arranged a bank loan, hired two workers and obtained a trade licence. Which stage of the entrepreneurial journey is shown?
items.answer: Mobilising resources
items.markingKey: (c) Mobilising resources. Money, people and permissions are being arranged.

items.stem:
Meera has just launched a mobile repair shop in Mysuru.
(i) State three challenges she may face in the coming months.
items.answer: (i) Finding customers; competition; arranging finance; hiring skilled staff; uncertainty (any three).
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Finding customers; competition; arranging finance; hiring skilled staff; uncertainty (any three).

items.stem: Manish took an aptitude test and listed his strengths and interests to decide what kind of business suits him. Which stage of the entrepreneurial journey is shown? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Self-discovery. Manish is trying to understand his own interests and strengths.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Self-discovery; 2 marks for the justification: Manish is trying to understand his own interests and strengths.

items.stem:
Om loved cooking and was good with people. He noticed that office workers in Kochi wanted home-style lunches. After comparing three ideas, he chose a tiffin service, wrote a plan, borrowed ₹2 lakh, hired two cooks and began deliveries in June. A year later he expanded to two more areas.
(i) Identify the stages of the entrepreneurial journey in the case, in order.
items.answer: (i) Self-discovery (loved cooking, good with people); identifying opportunities (office workers' need); generating and selecting ideas (compared three ideas); preparing a business plan; mobilising resources (loan, cooks); launching (deliveries in June); growth and scaling up (two more areas).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Self-discovery (loved cooking, good with people); identifying opportunities (office workers' need); generating and selecting ideas (compared three ideas); preparing a business plan; mobilising resources (loan, cooks); launching (deliveries in June); growth and scaling up (two more areas).

items.answer: An analysis of whether an idea is technically, financially and commercially workable.

items.stem: State any three criteria for selecting a business idea.

items.stem: Explain "Quantity is welcome" with reference to the rules of brainstorming.
items.answer: Quantity is welcome: The more ideas, the better the chance of a good one.

items.stem:
Riya found that customers want low-cost solar lamps, but the solar cells she needs are not available locally and must be imported at a high cost.
(i) Which type of feasibility is weak? (ii) Suggest one way to deal with it.
items.answer: (i) Technical feasibility (also financial, due to high cost). (ii) Find another supplier or technology, import in bulk, or tie up with a manufacturer.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Technical feasibility (also financial, due to high cost). (ii) Find another supplier or technology, import in bulk, or tie up with a manufacturer.

items.stem:
Harpreet wants to start a unit making millet-based snacks in Delhi. He has found suppliers of millets and a suitable machine, estimates a project cost of ₹12 lakh, and believes health-conscious young people will buy the snacks.
(i) Identify the three types of feasibility in the case. (ii) What else should he check under market feasibility?
items.answer: (i) Technical (suppliers, machine); financial (project cost); market (health-conscious buyers). (ii) Size of the market, competition, price customers will pay, distribution.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Technical (suppliers, machine); financial (project cost); market (health-conscious buyers). (ii) Size of the market, competition, price customers will pay, distribution.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A diagram that places a central idea in the middle with related ideas branching out from it."
items.answer: Mind-mapping
items.markingKey: (d) Mind-mapping: A diagram that places a central idea in the middle with related ideas branching out from it.

items.stem: Tara studies how many rival gyms exist in her area and what they charge. Which type of feasibility is being studied?

items.stem:
Students of a school in Chandigarh wanted to start a small business. They first listed every idea anyone could think of without judging, then drew a chart around 'school needs', and finally compared the ideas on demand, resources and profit.
(i) Identify the three steps or techniques used. (ii) State two rules of the first technique. (iii) State one more criterion they could use.
items.answer: (i) Brainstorming; mind-mapping; screening and selection of ideas. (ii) No criticism; quantity is welcome; wild ideas encouraged; build on others' ideas (any two). (iii) Competition / risk involved / personal interest and skills.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Brainstorming; mind-mapping; screening and selection of ideas. (ii) No criticism; quantity is welcome; wild ideas encouraged; build on others' ideas (any two). (iii) Competition / risk involved / personal interest and skills.

Gauri and Aditi plan to start a packaged-juice company in Varanasi, sell in several states, and use the brand name 'FreshSip'. They want limited liability and later plan to bring in investors.
(i) Suggest a suitable legal form. (ii) List four registrations or licences they need.
items.answer: (i) Private limited company (limited liability; can issue shares to investors). (ii) Certificate of incorporation; PAN and TAN; GST registration (inter-state supply); FSSAI licence; trademark registration for 'FreshSip'; Udyam registration (any four).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Private limited company (limited liability; can issue shares to investors). (ii) Certificate of incorporation; PAN and TAN; GST registration (inter-state supply); FSSAI licence; trademark registration for 'FreshSip'; Udyam registration (any four).

items.stem: Distinguish between an idea and an opportunity on the basis of value, meaning and test.
items.answer: (i) Value: an idea: may or may not be workable; an opportunity: commercially workable. (ii) Meaning: an idea: a thought about a possible product or service; an opportunity: an idea with real demand that can be met profitably. (iii) Test: an idea: not yet tested; an opportunity: tested for feasibility.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Value: an idea: may or may not be workable; an opportunity: commercially workable. (ii) Meaning: an idea: a thought about a possible product or service; an opportunity: an idea with real demand that can be met profitably. (iii) Test: an idea: not yet tested; an opportunity: tested for feasibility.

items.stem: Manish compared ten ideas on demand, cost and risk, and kept only two. Which technique of idea generation is being used?
items.answer: Screening of ideas
items.markingKey: (b) Screening of ideas. Weak ideas are dropped against criteria.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the business plan is correct?
items.answer: A business plan helps in raising funds.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: A business plan helps in raising funds.
options: A business plan helps in raising funds.
The organisational plan contains the advertising budget.
A business plan is prepared after the business closes.
A business plan has no use once funds are raised.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Pillai Stores needs ₹500 crore for a steel plant and wants to raise it from the public. (a) Which form of business organisation is most suitable? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Public company (b) It can invite the public to subscribe.
items.markingKey: (a) Public company, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: It can invite the public to subscribe.

items.stem:
Om is preparing a business plan for an organic grocery store in Pune. He has written about the products, the customers he will target, the shop's layout and suppliers, and the loan he needs.
(i) Identify four components he has covered. (ii) Which component should come first, and why?
items.answer: (i) Description of the business; marketing plan; operational plan; financial plan. (ii) Executive summary: it gives a quick overview that catches the investor's interest.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Description of the business; marketing plan; operational plan; financial plan. (ii) Executive summary: it gives a quick overview that catches the investor's interest.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Customer complaints are a good source of business ideas.
Reason (R): Complaints show needs that are not being met.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
